title: Chapter 3 — First Pay
description: A week behind the counter at Ọjà, a rival with a sharp tongue, the first wage, and what Emeka does with it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your first week at Ike's shop. You learn that a brake pad has four prices: the Igbo price, the Lagos price, the "my brother" price, and the price for a man in a hurry.

beats.speaker: ngozi
beats.text: (from the stall opposite, arms folded) New boy. You are holding that shock absorber like a baby. It is not a baby. It is a shock absorber. Sell it like one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Mama Ngozi has sold genuine parts at Ọjà for twenty-two years. She calls Ike "Mr Original" and does not mean it kindly.

beats.speaker: ngozi
beats.text: Watch the customer, not the part. A man who came in a taxi will pay. A man who came on foot will count. A man who came with his wife will buy the expensive one so she sees.

good.toast: Ike counts the till twice. "You get mouth. Good."

bad.toast: Mama Ngozi laughs at you from across the road. Loudly.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (Friday evening, peeling notes off a roll) Fifteen thousand. Your first Lagos money. Don't spend it on something stupid. Spend it on something smart, that looks stupid.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Fifteen thousand naira. In the village it was a month. In Lagos it is a week, if you don't eat meat.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The notes are still warm from Ike's pocket.

options.text: Send ₦10,000 to Nne. The oil women are still waiting.
Save all of it. Lagos eats people who don't save.
Buy a smartphone. A Lagos man without a camera is a ghost.

beats.speaker: ngozi
beats.text: (crossing the road with her arms folded) Before you spend it. Ike sells fakes, everybody knows. I want to know if YOU know. Twenty boxes. Tell me which ones are original.

won.toast: Mama Ngozi takes your hand and turns it over. "Quarry hands. Good eyes." She doesn't say anything else. She doesn't need to.

lost.toast: "You will learn," she says, "or you will become Ike." She goes back to her stall.

beats.objective: Find the old agbero with three fingers at Mallam Garba's tea.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: The JJC from the night bus. Still alive. Good. Sit. Garba, two teas, he's paying.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Rule number two: Lagos is not a city. It is a road with people on it. Learn the road, and the road will hide you when you need hiding.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: I can show you the back ways. Under the bridge, through the market, behind the motor park. Free. I like your face.

options.text: "I'm too busy, sir. Ike keeps me till ten."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three evenings. Prof walks slowly and talks fast. By the end you can cross Iyana-Wahala without touching the main road once.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Midnight. The shop floor. A carton for a mattress. Your phone lights up.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: The oil women came. I paid them. I told them my son sent it from Lagos and I watched their faces. (She laughs.) Thank you, my son.

variants.text: The oil women came again. I told them next week. They are tired of my next weeks. (She is not complaining. She is reporting, like weather.)

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: (a voice note) So? How is Lagos? Have you seen the sea? Are the buildings as tall as Ike says? Tell me true.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: She will play your answer three times. She always does.

options.text: Tell her the truth: cartons, rats, sixteen-hour days, and the sea once from a bus.
"It's beautiful. I'm doing well. Very soon, I'll send for you."

beats.title: First Pay
beats.summary: Fifteen thousand naira, a rival who teaches you for free, and an old man who knows every back road. Lagos is a road with people on it. You are on it now.
